page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is a shared-core virtual server configuration deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 x86_64 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The CPU microarchitecture provides 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, SHA extensions, and hardware AES acceleration. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and each instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread processing capabilities, with both stress-ng single-core performance and Geekbench single-core testing scoring in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded compression workflows also exhibit notable throughput, reaching top-tier ratings in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Geekbench text processing registers a strong result within the top 25%. However, due to its low total core count and shared CPU allocation, multi-threaded metrics scale more modestly: stress-ng multi-core and static web serving throughput register as average (middle 50%), while Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU scores, and Clang compilation fall into the bottom 25%.

Memory throughput exhibits divergence based on allocation size. While large uncached 256 MB block read and write speeds perform within the average tier, small cached blocks and overall PassMark memory scores register in the bottom quartiles. In-memory throughput for key-value stores like Redis SET operations and PassMark database operations also fall within the lower 25%. Small language model inference (135M) achieves average processing throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers an entry-level compute profile suitable for budget-conscious hosting where high single-threaded performance is required. UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is well-positioned for light web serving, basic microservices, single-threaded batch scripts, lightweight APIs, and development environments that do not require sustained multi-core parallelization or large memory footprints.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is a compact KVM-based cloud instance featuring 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM and 50 GB of local SSD storage. The underlying hardware incorporates advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and hardware AES cryptography. Synthetic benchmarks show standout single-threaded performance, ranking in the top 10% for single-core Geekbench, stress-ng, and data compression workloads. However, the dual-core shared configuration exhibits tradeoffs in highly parallel operations, ranking in the lower 25% for PassMark multi-core benchmarks, software compilation, and in-memory key-value operations. System memory bandwidth delivers middle-tier throughput for large sequential blocks but lower scores for cached transactions. This hardware setup suits lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing scripts, API endpoints, and low-footprint application environments.
